LLM_description:
Situation:
Brigade combat operations are ongoing in a contested sector. Supply Depot Bravo (rear) and Forward Supply Point Charlie (forward) must sustain dispersed supported units, including Forward Operating Base Alpha, 2nd Cavalry Troop, 3rd Infantry Battalion, Artillery Battery Delta, Engineer Company Echo, and Recon Platoon Foxtrot. Ground lines of communication run through a valley corridor, a ridgeline pass, and an urban axis. Each corridor presents distinct hazards: IEDs and ambush risk in the valley, rockfall and limited maneuver space on the pass, and civilian congestion and sniper threat in the urban axis. Road clearance, escort, and route surveillance assets are limited and must be prioritized. Weather and periodic curfews constrain movement windows and increase transit times. The fleet is available for ground distribution of a single critical supply class; aerial resupply is not authorized for routine sustainment.

Mission:
Move required supply from Supply Depot Bravo and Forward Supply Point Charlie to the supported units over the planning horizon to meet operational demand while minimizing total cost. Total cost includes transport costs, shortage penalty costs for any authorized shortfall, vehicle deployment costs, and fixed route security risk costs. Maintain the ability to mass combat power by keeping critical units resupplied and avoiding unnecessary exposure on high-risk routes.

Execution/Concept:
- We will plan daily flows from each depot to each unit. Outbound shipments from a depot will not exceed that depot’s available stock for the day and the supply type.
- Unit demand must be covered by inbound flows; if demand cannot be fully met, controlled shortfalls are permitted and will incur shortage penalties. Shortfalls are to be minimized and only accepted where the incremental risk or transport cost outweighs the penalty.
- Vehicle allocation will be integer, by route and day. The cargo volume moved on any depot-to-unit leg will not exceed the product of fleet capacity and vehicles committed to that leg, considering the volume per unit of supply.
- Routes must be explicitly activated before any vehicles can move. Activating a route on a given day (sending any vehicles) incurs a fixed Risk Cost that represents the escort teams, route clearance, overwatch, and ISR support required. This fixed Risk Cost applies once per activated route-day regardless of how many vehicles use the route.
- Total vehicles employed across all routes on a given day will not exceed the fleet available.
- Transport costs vary by depot-to-unit leg and reflect time-distance and terrain. Risk costs vary by route and reflect the security overhead described above. Vehicle deployment costs reflect operating, maintenance, and crew burden per vehicle-day.
- Priority of effort: sustain fire-capable units and maneuver battalions first, then engineer and reconnaissance elements. Consolidate shipments to reduce the number of activated routes where feasible, balancing against depot capacity, delivery windows, and unit demand urgency.
- Movement control will synchronize departures to exploit cleared windows, reduce exposure on high-risk segments, and deconflict convoys. EOD, route clearance, and escort assets will be tasked only to routes selected for activation on that day.
